title: Triangular-prism surface area
observableEvidence: Uses a text-described net of a triangular prism to identify all faces and finds total surface area in square units.
prompt: A triangular prism net has two congruent right-triangle faces with legs 3 cm and 4 cm, and three rectangular faces measuring 5 by 10 cm, 3 by 10 cm, and 4 by 10 cm. Find the total surface area.
solutionRepresentation: The two triangles have total area 2(1/2 x 3 x 4) = 12 square centimeters. The rectangles total 5 x 10 + 3 x 10 + 4 x 10 = 120 square centimeters. Total surface area is 132 square centimeters.
solutionMethod: Find both triangular-face areas and all three rectangular-face areas, then add the five net-face areas.

hintSteps.prompt: A triangular-prism net contains two triangles and three rectangles.
hintSteps.question: Which faces have area 1/2 times base times height, and which use length times width?

hintSteps.prompt: Surface area covers faces, so the final unit is a squared length unit.
hintSteps.question: What kind of unit should describe a face-area total?

accessibilityNotes: List the two triangular faces and three rectangular faces in text; no net drawing is required.
accessibleAlternative: Read aloud or display: A triangular prism net has two right triangles with legs three and four, plus rectangles five by ten, three by ten, and four by ten centimeters. Find total square centimeters.
